title: operator helm apply stalemate during sidecar migration causing tenant KV divergence and ingress failures
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Summary: During a private (VPC/on‑prem) control plane upgrade that migrates the operator sidecar to a new image + init ordering, several tenants observed their ingress routes fail and request latency spikes. Investigation shows the Helm post-upgrade phase occasionally stalls when a nodeagent crash coincides with a Helm hook ordering change, leaving partial CRDs and an out-of-sync KV store that the operator's reconciler doesn't detect. This ticket tracks the hotfix, rollout plan, customer communication, and runbook updates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start operator upgrade v3.3.x -> v3.4.1 on a multi-tenant onprem cluster with sidecar-migration flag enabled; 2) Simulate nodeagent OOM/crash during helm post-upgrade hook window; 3) Observe helm release in 'post-upgrade' state while operator reconciliation loops show idempotent-apply errors; 4) Confirm tenant ingress routes return 503/timeout and KV entries (tenant.{id}.manifest) differ from expected; 5) Observe increased reconcile latency and operator requeue storms.
observed_behavior: Helm apply enters a stalled state for some releases; operator logs show "reconcile: write failed: partial apply" and repeated restarts; nodeagent heartbeat missing triggers KV resync path that is no-op for certain keys; tenants report 503s and steady token costs increase due to retries.
root_cause: Race between Helm hook ordering (post-upgrade hooks assuming sidecar alive) and nodeagent crash during image rotation; operator reconciler treated the partially-applied CR set as final and did not re-trigger a full manifest replay. The combination produced durable kv-schema divergence for a subset of tenant manifests.
mitigation_and_short_term_fix: 1) Emergency customer-safe rollback script and rolling restart playbook (runbook attached); 2) Release operator-3.4.1-hotfix with a guard: detect 'partial-helm-apply' sentinel and force full manifest replay on reconcile; 3) Backfill a pre-upgrade 'lock' that prevents Helm post-upgrade hooks from assuming sidecar availability; 4) Ops guidance to increase nodeagent pod restart priority during upgrade windows.
long_term_remediation: 1) Add transactional-apply semantics to Helm orchestrator (idempotent two-phase apply with explicit finalizer); 2) Improve operator reconciliation to validate KV parity checksums after upgrades and auto-repair divergences; 3) Add preflight checks in console that detect nodeagent resource pressure and delay upgrade; 4) Add telemetry metric 'upgrade.partial_apply_count' and dashboarding/alerts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hotfix operator-3.4.1-hotfix deployed to canary tenant and passes gated e2e with simulated nodeagent crash; 2) Automated runbook validates rollback and tenant state recovered to parity in <= 15 minutes; 3) Post-deploy canary metrics show zero partial_apply occurrences for 24h; 4) Customer-affected tenants report restored ingress and no data loss.
test_plan: Unit tests for 'partial-apply' sentinel detection; integration test that simulates helm hook stall and validates full manifest replay; chaos e2e that injects nodeagent crash during upgrade; canary rollout to 3 low-risk tenants then progressive ramp.
rollout_plan: 1) Build and publish operator-3.4.1-hotfix image; 2) Deploy to internal staging clusters; 3) Canary deploy to 3 low-impact customers during maintenance window (03:00-06:00 UTC); 4) Monitor dashboards and rollback if partial_apply_count > 0 or ingress errors > baseline; 5) Progressive rollout across Dedicated and Private clusters over 48 hours.
communication: Customer email templates prepared for affected tenants (see Confluence); urgent status page entries to be posted while remediation ongoing; SE team notified—priority escalation channel open.
